transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been dealing with an intense, overwhelming fear of animals, especially dogs and spiders. It has been going on for almost two years now—about a year and ten months, to be exact. I felt it was finally time to seek some help for it.
Did this fear start after a frightening or traumatic event involving an animal, or has it been more of a persistent fear without a specific event causing it?
To be honest, I'm not really sure how it all started. I don't recall any specific traumatic event or bad experience with an animal that triggered it.
Outside of animals, do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of life, like work, health, or family, on most days? Or is the anxiety mainly limited to animals?
No, I don't worry about things like work, health, or my family at all. My anxiety is strictly focused on my intense fear of animals. Other than that, I feel completely normal.
Do you go out of your way to avoid dogs, spiders, or places where you might encounter them, and has this fear interfered with your daily life?

Yes, I actively go out of my way to avoid them, like taking long detours to bypass parks or refusing to visit friends who have pets. This constant avoidance has severely disrupted my daily routine and really restricted my social life.
When you do encounter a dog or spider, do you feel immediate intense fear or physical panic symptoms like a racing heart, shaking, or shortness of breath?

Yes, absolutely. The very moment I see a dog or a spider, I am hit with an immediate, overwhelming wave of terror. My heart starts racing instantly, I begin to shake all over, and I feel like I can't catch my breath.

Generalized Anxiety Disorder is not supported because the patient denies excessive worry in other domains, and there is no evidence here for trauma-based, psychotic, mood, eating, OCD-spectrum, or ADHD conditions from the allowed list.
